chapter: Violin, the 1936 tour and the photo
title: The band's theme song and the first tunes Lawrence learned
summary: Lawrence names his theme song, the first piece he learned (Hiawatha), and other early tunes he tries to recall.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And that Purple Rose of Cairo is theme song. No. Our theme song was Say a Little Prayer to Me. Was what? Say a Little Prayer for Me. That was our theme song. Oh, I wanted to get some of the early, you know? I didn't know.
I didn't know. It was our theme song. It was our theme song.
It was Say a Little Prayer for Me.
It was our theme song. Oh, I wanted to get some of the early tunes they played, the names of them when you were
first taught them. Do you remember the names of any of them? Oh, I see. It's kind of mixed up there now. Do you remember the first piece you learned?
The first piece I learned was that piece that my old boss used to play all the time. Lizzy on the Rails. I don't remember the real name of it, but that's what they used to call it.
Yeah? I never knew the right name.
I have a record of it. It's pretty jammed. I like that.
Yeah. Watermill and Vine, I think that's one of the numbers we played.
Meet me by the Watermill and Vine, my lending loop?

Uh-huh, and meet the old cherry on the... Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Well, I can remember a piece that we used to play, it was not right after... When I first began to play, Here Come Your Daddy Now. Roby Sho used to play, I remember too. Here Come Your Daddy Now, Oh Pop, Oh Pop, Oh Pop. Or So Mom, or something like that. Uh-huh. We used to play that, uh... Not when I first began, though. It was maybe a little while ago. I'll tell you what, if I can think of some of this. Every once in a while, uh... When I think of a piece that I used to play, I write down the name, you know? And then when I got the name, I can kind of memorize how it goes, and I come back here and practice it. Wait for it.

Well, why don't you write those down and then drop me a postcard next time you're coming to New Orleans, and I'll wait by the telephone at work, you know? I can... Yeah. Just write me that you've come and what time, and when you'll phone me at my work number. Yeah. I'll be up there working, you know?
